title: Quantized files: fp8, GGUF, and how loaders treat them
hook: Same model, three kinds of file, three different roads through the loader. And why you merge first and quantize after, measured.

verified.claim: UNETLoader's weight_dtype offers default, fp8_e4m3fn, fp8_e4m3fn_fast and fp8_e5m2, and these set the dtype in model_options.
unet_dtype keeps a file's fp8 if the card computes fp8, or if twice the parameters would not fit.
A native quantized file is a normal safetensors file with a comfy_quant tensor per module, holding JSON.
Core's model folders do not list .gguf, and main.py's warning recommends native formats to GGUF users.
The GGUF pack we read defines its own layers on comfy.ops.manual_cast and decodes weights when a layer is called.
verified.ref: calcuis/gguf pig.py, read as text and not run

verified.claim: Merge-order errors in the Lab come from a run here with real torch fp8 on synthetic weights.

unchecked: We did not run any GGUF pack, and we read only one. Others may differ.
The speed statement in main.py is the developers'. We did not test it.
The merge errors are on synthetic weights with fp8 and a single scale. Pictures, and finer formats, were not tested.
